sections.h2: Which selling routes work best for a Union City homeowner?
sections.html:
Owners here usually pick among an agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner approach, and a direct purchase by a cash buyer. The cash route wins on speed when the house needs work, carries a tax balance or has tenants in it.

Union City lies in southern Fulton County, so most paperwork passes through Fulton offices plus the city's Community Development and Finance departments. Sorting those out first shortens nearly any sale.

  • Pull your deed and the current mortgage payoff statement.
  • Look for open building permits or code citations tied to the address.
  • Make sure city and county taxes are paid up.
  • Gather HOA documents if your street has covenants.

Cash offers generally come in below a repaired and staged listing, and the exchange is certainty and speed. Weigh what you would net after repairs, carrying costs and an agent's commission against the quick close.

sections.h2: What does Union City's location mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The city calls itself a small community in the southern part of Fulton County, roughly fifteen minutes from Atlanta and ten miles from Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. Buyers who commute or fly often tend to value that airport distance.

Union City also holds a Camera Ready City designation and points to Atlanta Metro Studios as one of the region's large production facilities. The Census lists transportation and warehousing receipts of $439,256 thousand for 2022 in Union City.

Population has climbed: 19,456 residents in the 2010 census, 26,830 in the 2020 census, and an estimate of 29,910 for July 1, 2025. Land area was 19.67 square miles in 2020, against 19.11 in 2010, so new households arrived inside a nearly fixed footprint.

Among its other designations, Union City lists Purple Heart City, AARP Community and City of Ethics, and it says it was selected for the Georgia Initiative for Community Housing to work with state partners on housing options. The Census puts civilian labor force participation at 68.5 percent of residents aged 16 and over, and 70.5 percent among women, which points to a working-age population that may need to relocate for jobs.

sections.h2: Which Union City housing figures matter for pricing a sale?
sections.html:
Owners occupy 40.4 percent of Union City homes by the Census count, which makes rental houses a big slice of the market. Numbers are 2020 to 2024 survey estimates unless dated.

sections.h2: How are Union City property taxes billed?
sections.html:
The city's own taxes ride on the Fulton County bill. Its Finance page gives the 2026 millage rate as 11.296, split into 11.132 for maintenance and operations and 0.164 for bonds.

The city says existing homestead, disability, disabled veteran and senior exemptions on city taxes stay in place without a new application, and that new Senior Homestead applications go to Fulton County directly. The city itself still collects unpaid 2024 and earlier balances, which can carry interest, penalties and tax sale proceedings.

Fulton splits the work in two. The Board of Assessors keeps ownership and mailing records, sets values and takes homestead applications and appeals. The Tax Commissioner builds the bill and collects payment.

  • Fulton County Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100
  • Fulton County Board of Assessors: 404-612-6440

Clear any older city balance on your parcel before closing, since the title search will surface it.

sections.h2: How does a Fulton assessment appeal work for Union City owners?
sections.html:
Fulton owners get 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. The 2026 notices were posted online on June 19, 2026, and the county named Friday, July 31, 2026 as the deadline for most owners unless the notice shows another date. That 2026 window has closed.

Only the assessed value can be appealed, and the estimated tax cannot. File online at the county assessor site, in person or by mail, then pick a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer, where fees may apply for the last two. Appeals can take months, and a temporary tax bill may arrive during the wait. Pay it, or penalties follow.

The South Fulton Service Center of the Board of Assessors sits at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224, and the phone is 404-612-6440. The county calls April 1 the standard homestead deadline, with a second window during the appeal period for owners who qualified as of January 1.

sections.h2: Which Union City permit and code rules touch a sale?
sections.html:
Most construction needs a building permit from the city, and work starts only once it is issued. A permit lapses when construction fails to begin within 180 days or stops for 180 consecutive days.

Permit applications, plan submittals, invoice payment and inspection scheduling run through the city's IWORQ online portal. Inspection requests need the permit number and contractor code, and requests for next-business-day inspection must come in before 4:00 pm Eastern. The Community Development office is at 5041 Union St, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and permit questions go to 770-515-7950, option 1.

Code Enforcement accepts violations by phone, fax, email or area survey, and an officer investigates within 24 hours of a report. Its phone line is (770) 515-7890, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Officers inspecting one property may also survey adjacent properties for violations, so a neighbor's complaint can lead to a look at your yard.

The Planning Division posts the current zoning ordinance, development regulations and subdivision regulations, along with the Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use Map. Look up the zoning on your parcel if a buyer plans a particular use.

sections.h2: How do recording and transfer tax work on a Union City sale?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court once Georgia's transfer tax is paid. Liability falls on the seller unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The state's printed rate sits on its Department of Revenue page.

Fulton County Schools serves Union City. Its South Learning Center is at 4025 Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district publishes an address lookup showing the elementary, middle and high school zones for any home. Share that result when a buyer asks.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Union City?
faqs.a: Fulton County sends one bill that carries the city portion. The city's Finance page gives 2026 millage as 11.296 and says delinquent balances from 2024 and earlier stay with the city.

faqs.q: Is a city inspection required before I sell in Union City?
faqs.a: The permit pages do not list one. They do require permits for most construction and run inspections through the online portal, so confirm that past work was permitted and signed off.

faqs.q: What if I miss the Fulton assessment appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The right to appeal that year's value is lost once the printed date passes. For 2026 the county named July 31 for most owners. Watch the date on next year's notice and file early online or at a Board of Assessors office.

faqs.q: Can I report a code problem next door before I list?
faqs.a: Yes. Reports go in by phone at (770) 515-7890, fax, email or through an area survey during an inspection, and an officer looks into it within 24 hours. Clearing an eyesore early helps showings.

faqs.q: Which district serves Union City homes?
faqs.a: Fulton County Schools. Its South Learning Center is on Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district's address lookup shows the elementary, middle and high school zones for your house.
